payload.headline: Netflix slips below its own-history floor; small buy holds, add at 58.22

summary.thesis: A grade B business with growing free cash flow trades below every method's middle fair value, but sales growth is slowing and the margin sits at a five-year peak.
summary.decision: Long-term: keep a small buy and add only at 58.22. Swing: no trade while the downtrend holds.
summary.act_at: small buy near 58.46, add at 58.22, no buying above 62.93

payload.happening: Netflix fell 2.27% to 58.46. It is in a downtrend below its falling 20-, 50- and 200-day averages (62.74, 67.82, 80.06), and our data lists no support below the price. Netflix, Amazon and Fox are reported to be bidding for the 2030 men's World Cup rights, with Disney out. The next earnings report is on 2027-01-19.
payload.business: The business is still strong. Over the last twelve months revenue was 49.7B, up from 43.4B. Free cash flow (cash left after running and investing in the business) was 11.4B, up from 9.0B. Operating margin rose to 31.3% from 29.14%. The share count fell 3.35% in a year, so each share owns more of the company. Two things are at risk. First, growth is slowing: quarterly sales growth was 11.85%, down from 16.19% two quarters ago. Second, the filings note that a 31% margin is at the top of the 5-year range of 17–31%, and peaks like that usually fade. Analysts cut this quarter's EPS estimate by 7.3% over 30 days. The World Cup bid is a report only. A win would bring live-sports demand but also large rights costs that could weigh on margins (general knowledge). Today it changes sentiment, not the numbers. The balance sheet is not a problem: debt of 12.7B against 8.2B cash leaves net debt of 4.4B, which is small next to 11.4B of yearly free cash flow.

worth.text: At 58.46 the stock trades at 16.6 times trailing earnings and 15.5 times next year's. Its price-to-sales ratio is 4.8, against a peer median of 7.0, and sits at the 20th percentile of its own 5-year history. The DCF (a model that values future cash flows in today's money) gives 37.15 bear, 62.93 base and 74.99 bull. Own-history price-to-sales gives 59.82 to 122.15. The price implies free cash flow starts growing at 12.7% a year. At 10% starting growth the value is 52.3, and at 20% it is 77.98. The gap between the methods comes down to one question: do the old, higher sales multiples come back, or does the cash-flow model hold? The DCF ignores past multiples, so it sits far below the own-history middle of 84.5. Margins are the main risk. If operating margin falls to 23%, the value is 58.22, about today's price. At 15% it is 38.45.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow starts growing between 10% and 20% a year, around the 12.7% the price implies, while operating margin does not fall much below 23%.

bull: Free cash flow grew to 11.4B from 9.0B, a 22.87% free-cash-flow margin.
Price-to-sales of 4.8 is below the peer median of 7.0 and at the 20th percentile of its own 5-year history.
The share count shrank 3.35% in a year, and operating margin rose to 31.3% from 29.14%.
bear: Quarterly sales growth slowed to 11.85% from 16.19% two quarters ago.
Analysts cut this quarter's EPS estimate by 7.3% in 30 days, and next year's by 1.1%.
If operating margin falls from today's 5-year-high 31.3% to 15%, the value drops to 38.45.

levels.what: Low end of the own-history price-to-sales range. The price is now below it, so a small first position fits here.
Value if operating margin falls to 23%. At this price the margin-peak risk is already priced in, so this is the level to add.
DCF base value. Above it the margin of safety is gone, so no buying there.

longterm.why: A grade B business trades below the DCF base of 62.93 and below its own-history low of 59.82. Estimates are still falling and no support is listed, so the position starts small and grows only at 58.22.

swing.why: The trend is down, with lower highs and lower lows below the falling 20-day average of 62.74. Resistance sits at 61.15–61.63 and 64.56–65.08, and no support is listed below. No trade until the stock closes above the 64.56–65.08 zone.

decision.timing: The 2027-01-19 report falls before the 2027-02-19 option expiry, and options price a move of about 16.9% by then. Before the report, keep the small first position and add only at 58.22 or after a report that holds operating margin near 31.3%.

change_mind: The 2027-01-19 report shows operating margin below 29.14% or quarterly sales growth below 11.85%: move from buy to wait.
Next-year EPS consensus falls below the 3.56 low estimate: stop adding, even at 58.22.
A close above the 64.56–65.08 resistance zone: turn the swing call to enter.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still buy; the 2.27% drop to 58.46 took the price below the 59.82 own-history floor but not to the 58.22 add level (today's data moves yesterday's 59.68, 58.03 and 62.64 to 59.82, 58.22 and 62.93).
payload.label: Research, not advice.
